I opened this thread for further discussion and collaboration started from PR #37310 by @Yongxi Lin (Aaron). The goal there is to prove that (normalized) Hausdorff measure restricted to the sphere coincides with the spherical measure. It likely needs the coarea formula for Hausdorff measure to calculate the area of a sphere.

I happened to also work on related formula in my branch https://github.com/wwylele/mathlib4/tree/area-formula, following the book Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions. I'd like to confirm that this is also the approach you have in mind, and learn whether you also have some work done so we can de-duplicate the effort.

You also mentioned needing to prove IsOpenPosMeasure and IsLocallyFiniteMeasure for the Hausdorff measure on the sphere. I haven't got concrete idea how to approach these yet. Do you have a proof in the literature to follow?

I don't have any progress on the (co)area formula. The book you mentioned is one of the standard references I know for geometric measure theory, so I think it is great you are following that book. I'll also spend some time later to think about what's the best way to formalize these formulae.

Regarding the last part, the idea is simple: suppose we have a Lipschitz m-dimensional manifold, then around every point we can find an open set U containing it that is biLipschitz homeomorphic to a bounded open set V of R^m, then as the m-dimensional Hausdorff of V is finite and positive, we can deduce that U also has finite and positive m-dimensional Hausdorff measure by LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le and its analogue for antiLipschitz mappings. Here's an outline for formalization:

  1. Similar to contDiffGroupoid, we define a groupoid of biLipschitz mappings
  2. Define a typeclass of Lipschitz manifolds, and show that IsManifold is a Lipschitz manifold.
  3. Formalize the proof above for Lipschitz manifolds.
  4. Deduce that the Hausdorff measure on the sphere IsOpenPosMeasure and IsLocallyFiniteMeasure by EuclideanSpace.instIsManifoldSphere and 2 (and actually as the sphere is compact, once we have shown that the measure is locally finite, the typeclass system should also be able to automatically infer that the measure is finite).
:+1: I think I understand this now on the paper. I'll take a deeper look at the manifold part of mathlib because last time when I tried I could hardly parse any of it...

That's also one of my concerns (as I am also not very familiar with that part of the library and I just started reading the documentation recently), I would actually appreciate if someone who are familiar with the manifold library can take a look of this outline and give me some advices, so that at least I know I am on the right track.

@Yongxi Lin (Aaron) I have got a proof of the area formula (only in the case of non-vanishing Jacobian) in #39120. Obviously it needs massive clean up but this feels like a good starting point.

In theory this can already be used to calculate area of sphere by parametrizing it, but it is more cumbersome than using the coarea formula. I haven't touched the coarea formula yet. It seems that it will be longer

One thing that I'd like people to chime in on is whether the proof should assume injectivity throughout.

One of the formula proved here (version A) is akin to docs#MeasureTheory.lintegral_abs_det_fderiv_eq_addHaar_image, with the following modification

  • f is allowed to have different domain and codomain E and F
  • E and F are restricted to inner product space
  • The measure μ is restricted to μHE
  • det is replaced by normDet defined in #37295

The book proved a seemingly more general version (version B) that doesn't require injectivity, which replaces the right hand side with ∫⁻ y, (s ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}).encard.toENNReal ∂(μHE[finrank ℝ U]), taking multiplicity into consideration. Version A is an immediate corollary from version B. In the other direction, one should be also be able to get version B from version A by partitioning a non-injective function into injective pieces, except they might encounter trouble when there are points with infinite multiplicity

I propose we formalize version A (requiring injectivity) first, which is the most useful one and has simpler proof, just like we have docs#MeasureTheory.lintegral_abs_det_fderiv_eq_addHaar_image that requires injectivity. The non-injective version can be added later on demand, and those potential difficulties on infinite multiplicity is usually not useful in practice anyway.
